q.t: Two lines intersect. One angle is 120°. What is the angle next to it (its linear pair)?
q.e: A linear pair sits on a straight line, so the two angles add to 180°: 180 − 120 = 60.

q.t: Two lines intersect and one angle is 70°. What is the vertically opposite angle?
q.e: Vertically opposite angles are always equal.

q.t: How many angles are formed when two lines intersect?
q.e: Around the crossing point there are four angles.

q.t: At most how many points can two different straight lines share?
q.e: Through two points there is only one straight line, so two different lines can meet at most once.

q.t: Lines that cross at 90° are called…
q.e: Perpendicular lines meet at right angles.

q.t: Lines in the same plane that never meet are called…
q.e: Parallel lines never meet however far they are extended.

q.t: A line that crosses two other lines is called a…
q.e: That's the definition of a transversal.

q.t: How many angles does a transversal make with two lines?
q.e: 4 angles at each of the 2 crossing points.

q.t: If two intersecting lines make four equal angles, each angle is…
q.e: The four angles fill a full turn (360°), so each is 360 ÷ 4 = 90°.

q.t: Linear-pair angles always add up to…
q.e: They make a straight line, which is 180°.

q.t: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One corresponding angle is 75°. The other is…
q.e: When lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal.

q.t: l ∥ m and an alternate angle is 48°. Its alternate partner is…
q.e: Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal.

q.t: l ∥ m and one interior angle on one side of the transversal is 50°. The other interior angle on the same side is…
q.e: Same-side interior angles between parallel lines add to 180°: 180 − 50 = 130.

q.t: A transversal crosses two lines. Can all 8 angles be different sizes?
o: No — vertically opposite angles are equal, so at most 4 sizes
Yes, if the lines are not parallel
No — they are always all equal
q.e: At each crossing the vertically opposite angles match, leaving at most 4 different sizes.

q.t: Corresponding angles made by a transversal on two lines are equal. What can we say about the lines?
q.e: Equal corresponding angles means both lines tilt the same way against the transversal, so they never meet.

q.t: Parallel lines and a transversal; one angle is 135°. What is the size of the other kind of angle?
q.e: Only two sizes appear, and they form linear pairs: 180 − 135 = 45°.

q.t: With two set-square perpendiculars to line l, why are the two lines parallel?
o: Both make 90° with l — equal corresponding angles
Because they are the same length
Because a set square is a triangle
q.e: l is a transversal; the corresponding angles are both 90°, so the lines are parallel.

q.t: A square sheet is folded in half horizontally. How many parallel horizontal lines (edges + crease) are there?
q.e: Top edge, bottom edge, and the new crease between them.

q.t: Which pair is ALWAYS equal, even if the two lines are not parallel?
q.e: Vertically opposite angles are equal at any crossing. The others need parallel lines.

q.t: If one angle at a crossing is 90°, how many of the four angles are 90°?
q.e: Its linear-pair partner is 180 − 90 = 90, and vertically opposite angles copy these two.

q.t: ∠a = 120° at line l. At line m, the angle corresponding to ∠a's linear-pair partner is 70°. Are l and m parallel?
o: Only if the transversal is perpendicular
q.e: ∠a's partner is 180 − 120 = 60°. Its corresponding angle is 70°, not 60°, so the lines aren't parallel.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠ADC = 60°. Find ∠DAB.
q.e: AB ∥ DC with transversal AD: same-side interior angles add to 180°.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠DAB = 120° and diagonal AC makes ∠DAC = 65°. Find ∠CAB.
q.e: ∠DAB is split by AC: 120 = 65 + ∠CAB.

q.t: Two parallel lines and a transversal. One angle is 3 times its linear-pair partner. The smaller angle is…
A path bends at a point between two parallel lines, making 40° with the top line and 68° with the bottom line. The bend angle is…
q.e: Draw a parallel line through the bend: it splits the bend into 40° and 68° (alternate angles). Total 108°.

q.t: Why are alternate angles equal when lines are parallel?
o: Each equals the same corresponding angle, via vertically opposite angles
Because the transversal is always perpendicular
q.e: ∠6 = ∠2 (corresponding) and ∠2 = ∠4 (vertically opposite), so ∠6 = ∠4.

q.t: Four angles at a crossing are x, 2x, x, 2x. What is x?
q.e: They fill a full turn: 6x = 360 → x = 60°.

q.t: A line drawn on the floor and one on the ceiling never meet. Are they parallel?
o: Not necessarily — parallel lines must lie in the same plane
Only if they are equal in length
q.e: The definition needs the same plane. Lines in different planes can miss each other without being parallel.

q.t: Folding a sheet horizontally in half three times (unfold each time), how many parallel lines do you see including the two edges?
q.e: 3 folds make 8 strips; lines = strips + 1 = 9.

q.t: Same-side interior angles between two lines are 85° and 85°. Are the lines parallel?
q.e: For parallel lines the pair must add to 180°. 85 + 85 = 170, so the lines lean towards each other.

q.t: Two angles in a linear pair differ by 40°. The bigger one is…
AB ∥ CD ∥ EF and ∠BEF = 55°. The same-side interior partner of ∠BEF is…
q.e: Interior angles on the same side add to 180°: 180 − 55 = 125°.

q.t: Parallel lines, transversal: one angle is (2x + 10)° and its corresponding angle is (3x − 20)°. Find x.
q.e: Corresponding angles are equal: 2x + 10 = 3x − 20 → x = 30 (both 70°).

q.t: Parallel lines, transversal: same-side interior angles are (x + 20)° and (2x + 10)°. Find x.
Of the 8 angles a transversal makes with two parallel lines, how many different sizes are there (if it is not perpendicular)?
q.e: Corresponding and vertically opposite angles match up so only two sizes remain, and they add to 180°.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 120°. What is ∠C (the opposite angle)?
q.e: ∠B = 180 − 120 = 60° (interior angles), and ∠C = 180 − 60 = 120°. Opposite angles are equal.

q.t: How can you be SURE two drawn lines are parallel?
o: Draw a transversal and check corresponding angles are equal
Check they are the same length
q.e: Equal corresponding angles is both needed and enough for lines to be parallel.

q.t: In a 'Z' shape between two parallel lines, the top angle is 37°. The bottom angle inside the Z is…
q.e: The angles inside a Z are alternate angles, equal when the lines are parallel.

q.t: Two lines cross. ∠a + ∠c = 140°, where ∠a and ∠c are vertically opposite. Find ∠b.
q.e: ∠a = ∠c = 70°. ∠b forms a linear pair with ∠a: 180 − 70 = 110°.

q.t: Why is the 'equal vertically opposite angles' fact a proof and not just an observation?
o: It follows from linear pairs adding to 180° for ANY angle
q.e: ∠a + ∠b = 180 and ∠b + ∠c = 180 for any ∠b, so ∠a = ∠c always — reasoning covers every case.
